T0609.title: Robot Operating System
T0609.definition: An open-source middleware framework for developing robot software, providing inter-node communication, hardware abstraction, and motion planning; the de-facto standard robot middleware.
T0609.description: The Robot Operating System (ROS/ROS2) is maintained by Open Robotics and implements publish-subscribe inter-node communication via the DDS (Data Distribution Service) middleware. ROS2's default DDS communication has no authentication and plaintext multicast; nodes can arbitrarily publish/subscribe to topics, and SROS2/DDS-Security is not enabled by default and implements only 3 of the 5 security SPIs. This makes ROS2 deployments face severe security risks: FastDDS heap overflow (CVE-2024-30259), 33 Nav2 CVEs, DDS Discovery leaking LAN node information, and rostopic eval() injection (CVE-2024-41921). ROS is the main attack surface for robot-middleware vulnerability exploitation.
T0609.usageExample: A warehouse robot developed on the Robot Operating System (ROS) without SROS2 enabled lets an attacker arbitrarily publish topics to tamper with navigation commands on the LAN.
